content.content:
A draft is reviewed through jj in the workspace where it is written. `deccy show` never renders a draft, and a draft never edits a node document: the draft is not a node and no document under `nodes/` is the draft, so review neither renders a draft from the node space nor writes one into it.

The review is read in the draft's own workspace because that is where the draft is. A draft's workspace lies under one per-user root outside the repository, at the directory derived from the record's handle (xqzstoyo), and each draft is written in its own workspace, so one directory holds one draft and no second writer shares it (znskspqs). What a reviewer reads there is jj's state in that working copy — the changes the draft has made and the history above them — and jj is the reader of jj's state. No second coordinate is needed to find it: the handle the record is keyed by fixes the directory (xqzstoyo), the record carries that workspace as a reference rather than the draft's content (owyntkvw), and the repository's own working copy is a different workspace, so neither the registry nor the trunk can be read as the draft. Reviewing is therefore opening that directory and reading the draft's changes in place; nothing is exported, copied or rendered first.

The review writes nothing. It is a reading of jj state in a workspace outside the repository (xqzstoyo), so it creates no node, no edge and no field, and it lands nothing: a draft is not a graph node (znskspqs), and what reaches the node is landing, which records a draft into its own node as its own operation (znskspqs) — a separate commitment this one does not decide. Nor does the review need a verb of its own: the draft's changes are already jj's state in its own workspace (xqzstoyo, znskspqs), and a deccy review verb would have to render draft content, which the show contract cannot carry (kywrtyoq, rnolplyu).

`show` never renders a draft because a draft is not in what show reads or writes. `deccy show <id>` reads the named nodes, locating each file the way edge targets resolve, and writes one output per valid node (kywrtyoq); the output is the stored node document as pretty JSON verbatim (rnolplyu). Its unit is the node: one output per valid node, the document the graph holds. A draft is not a graph node (znskspqs), and its identity is a registry-local handle that is neither a node id nor a change id — it is not listed with the nodes and not validated as a node (owyntkvw) — so a draft handle names nothing show resolves, and `show <handle>` has no valid node, so no draft can appear in its output (kywrtyoq, rnolplyu). The draft's absence is not a filter show learns to apply; it is the fact that the draft was never in the node set (owyntkvw). Nor can a node's own id render that node's open draft: show writes the stored document verbatim (rnolplyu), and the draft's content is not in the stored document, because the draft is a working copy in another workspace that has not been recorded into the node (xqzstoyo, znskspqs). And where one node carries several drafts — competing alternatives, or a redraft while an earlier draft is open — one output per valid node leaves show no draft to choose and no rule by which to choose one (znskspqs, kywrtyoq); the stored document is the answer that needs no choice.

A draft never edits a node document to be a draft. The record is not the document `nodes/<id>.json`, it is not listed with the nodes and their edges, and it is not validated as a node (owyntkvw); and a draft is not a graph node (znskspqs). There is accordingly no node document that is a draft: review opens none, creates none and amends none to hold the draft, to name it, or to record what a review saw, and nothing under `nodes/` gains a field from a review. What a draft does change is the content of the node it names (znskspqs) — its document included, when the decision is inline — and that is the named node's content changing in the draft's own workspace, recorded into that node's own operation when the draft lands (znskspqs), not the draft taking a document of its own. The distinction keeps `nodes/` the set of recorded decisions: a draft written into the node space would list a state the graph has not recorded, and show would then render it as stored (kywrtyoq, rnolplyu) although no recording had made it so.

These clauses are one commitment: the draft is reviewed where it is, and nowhere else. Its working copy is the draft's own copy, outside the repository at the directory the handle fixes (xqzstoyo), and it belongs to that draft alone (znskspqs); its identity is a registry-local handle that is not a node (owyntkvw); and show's output is the valid node's stored document (kywrtyoq, rnolplyu), so the node space can neither display a draft nor hold one. Take away the workspace and the review would have to read the registry, which carries references and not the draft's content (owyntkvw); take away the non-node identity and show would have to learn to read drafts, which its one-output-per-valid-node contract (kywrtyoq) and its verbatim stored document (rnolplyu) cannot express; take away the non-editing clause and a draft would appear under `nodes/` before it was recorded (owyntkvw, znskspqs). They answer one question — where and how a draft is reviewed — with one answer: in its own workspace, through jj, with the node space untouched.

Nothing here decides which jj commands a reviewer runs, how the workspace is created or removed or what a missing workspace means (xqzstoyo defers those), when a draft is open or lands or how landing records it (znskspqs fixes landing per draft; the commitment that owns it decides the rest), whether `show` reports an id it cannot resolve (rnolplyu speaks only for valid ids), or what any other reading of the registry reports — those belong to the commitments that own them.
content.rationale:
The review surface has to be chosen, and the choice follows the draft's own place. A draft's workspace is fixed by the record's handle under the user's root outside the repository (xqzstoyo) and each draft is written in its own workspace (znskspqs), so the draft's state is already jj state in one directory: the reviewer reads it there, in place, with no export and no second representation to keep in step. Any other surface would need a copy that can drift, or a lookup the repository cannot serve because the workspace lies outside it (xqzstoyo).

The node space cannot be that surface in either direction. `show` reads the named nodes and writes one output per valid node (kywrtyoq), each output the stored node document verbatim (rnolplyu); a draft is not a graph node (znskspqs), and its record is not a node document, is not listed with the nodes and is not validated as one (owyntkvw). So a handle names nothing show resolves, and a node's own id shows the node as stored rather than an open draft's changes — which is also what keeps show from having to choose among the several drafts one node may carry (znskspqs). In the other direction the review edits nothing under `nodes/`: a draft written into a node document would list an unrecorded state, and show would render it as stored (rnolplyu) although nothing had recorded it, so the review stays a reading of the draft's workspace and no node document gains a field from it.

The negatives are therefore one decision with the positive one: the review is jj's, in the draft's own workspace, and the graph is untouched — no review verb, no draft in `show`, no document under `nodes/` for a draft. A review verb or a show extension is excluded by the same facts: it would have to render draft content that neither the one-output-per-valid-node contract (kywrtyoq) nor the verbatim stored document (rnolplyu) can carry, would have to read the registry, which the record's non-node identity does not put in the node set (owyntkvw), and would have to pick a draft where the model allows a node several (znskspqs). Reviewing through jj where the draft is written is the arrangement in which every party already holds what it needs: the reviewer holds the handle (xqzstoyo), jj holds the changes, and the graph holds only what was recorded.

This node decides the review arrangement alone; which jj commands a reviewer runs, how a workspace is opened or removed (xqzstoyo), landing and its recording (znskspqs), and `show`'s behaviour outside its valid-id contract (rnolplyu) remain with the commitments that own them.
